items.title: The Incredible Art of Subtleties | Tudor Feasts at Hampton Court Palace
items.description:
The royal courts of Tudor England and 16th century Europe loved showing off with spectacular feasts and show-stopping foods. discovery_articles.title: The Afro-Antillean Museum in Panama City, Panama
discovery_articles.snippet: During the construction of the Panama Canal hundreds of thousands of workers were imported from Jamaica and other Caribbean islands and were settled in tenement housing on the outskirts of Panama City. Each house was constructed as small as possible, often no more than a wooden shack raised on posts to keep the insects out, with communal bathrooms and a zinc roof. It was in one of these tenement neighbourhoods, known then as Guachapalí, today as El Marañón, that canal workers constructed the Cristian Mission Chapel in their off hours, from 1909-1910.

featured_read.title: Dostoyevsky in Love
featured_read.snippet: “I love her happiness more than my own.”
featured_read.blurb: This piece sits with the uncomfortable truth that loving someone deeply can mean subordinating your own joy to theirs — and asks whether that selflessness is devotion or a quiet kind of disappearance. Dostoyevsky wrote some of the most tortured, luminous sentences about human longing, and here those sentences are turned on his own life.

news.title: Meera Sodha’s vegan recipe for cold tomato and tahini noodles with peanut, coriander and lime | The new vegan
news.snippet: This globetrotting cold fusion dish boasts south-east Asian, Middle-Eastern and even Italian influences, producing sweet and sour notes and a chilli kick Can a person in a heatwave ever have too many cold noodle dishes? I’d wager no – hence today’s recipe. It started life as one of my favourite meals, the mighty spaghetti pomodoro, but then packed its bags and travelled through the Middle East, picking up some tahini along the way, then on to Indonesia for some heat (sambal oelek), and then hopped over to Vietnam for a final hurrah of fresh lime, coriander and peanuts.
news.blurb: When a dish travels through Southeast Asia, the Middle East, and Italy before landing in your bowl, you know the flavour passport is well-stamped — a brilliant read for heat-wave recipe inspiration.
